title: Sporadic and rapidly progressive arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy in a 12-year-old boy who was diagnosed with epilepsy
case_prompt: A 12-year-old Syrian boy was brought to the pediatric emergency department with fatigue, dizziness, and palpitations. He had a history of recurrent seizures diagnosed as epilepsy based on EEG showing centro-parietal theta rhythmic activity with 2–3 Hz generalized waves and spikes, and he had been taking sodium valproate 500 mg twice daily. On examination, he was alert; blood pressure was 90/60 mm Hg, and the pulse was rapid and feeble. ECG showed sustained wide QRS tachycardia mimicking a left bundle branch block morphology in the superior axis. Intravenous amiodarone up to 15 mg/kg was ineffective, and synchronized DC cardioversion restored sinus rhythm. Laboratory studies, including complete blood count, electrolytes (K⁺, Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, Na⁺), creatinine, and TSH, were all within normal limits. A 12-lead ECG in sinus rhythm demonstrated right bundle branch block, T-wave inversion, and ε waves in leads V1 to V5. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed right ventricular structural alteration with blood stagnation; the parasternal short-axis RV outflow tract measured 35 mm, and there was regional right ventricular dyskinesia.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Metabolic and endocrine causes — “Blood tests revealed no signs of hyperthyroidism or ion disturbances, which could have caused palpitations.”  
2. Myocarditis and Chagas disease — “the absence of infection and associated symptoms in lab findings and in child’s medical history ruled out myocarditis and Chagas disease.”  
3. Sarcoidosis — “considering the rarity of childhood sarcoidosis, which is most frequently diagnosed between 20 and 29 years of age, we did not consider sarcoidosis as a potential cause.”  
4. Cardiac tuberculosis — “normal findings on chest X-ray and the absence of any signs of infection in the child or his family members made cardiac tuberculosis unlikely.”  
5. WPW syndrome, SVT, LQTS, and Brugada syndrome — “ECG findings ruled out Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome, supraventricular tachycardia (SVT), long QT syndrome (LQTS), and Brugada syndrome.”  
6. Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy — “characteristic ECG and TTE findings led us to consider a diagnosis of ARVC according to the modified Task Force Criteria.”
